subject: Task 21.12 — corrected release build, full suite, reproducible artifact, and release documentation
summary: Independent re-verification of every checkable claim in the task 21.12 worker report; no test, source, or build-metadata file was changed by this task, so nothing in the suite can have been silently weakened. 1) Reproducibility: a fourth clean build from my own git export of the working tree (1,125 tracked files, /tmp/final-review/test-quality/src, an absolute path the worker did not use, no .git/bin/obj/artifacts) ran './build.sh restore && ./build.sh build && ./build.sh package' and reproduced the recorded identity exactly: 619,861 bytes, SHA-256 2a039fc7075f4e4c1a1c785eb0b3757636fc0573da1361ee814cfd4099297268, MD5 631fbfa5a4fb58fac5a877eeef761193, 7 entries all stamped 2000-01-01 00:00, cmp byte-identical to the repository archive. My extraction's seven per-entry SHA-256 values match the release doc's table exactly. 2) Suite honesty: I independently reproduced all four documented tiers exactly — default with the corrected archive present 0 failed / 1,966 passed / 66 skipped / 2,032 total; default without the archive 0/1,963/69/2,032; host-guarded against the verified pinned host 0/1,986/46/2,032; forced-native with the pinned host's own native chain 0/2,053/21/2,074. The pinned host precondition was verified before the host-guarded run (/tmp/arrtags-14.3/jellyfin/Jellyfin.Api.dll present; /tmp/arrtags-14.3/console.log records 'Jellyfin version: 12.0.0'). The 66/69/46/21 skip taxonomy reconciles exactly to the source attribute counts (20 [JellyfinHostFact] + 41 [SkiaNativeFact] + 4 [SkiaNativeTheory] + 1 [NonCanonicalRuntimeFact] = 66, plus 3 [PackagedPluginFact] only when no archive is present), and every guard attribute assigns Skip only on the unset condition, so a set-but-broken environment fails rather than passes. No guard file changed since task 21.3 (git diff 079116e..HEAD over the five guard attributes is empty) and no skip was added or widened. 3) The +29 test-total delta over 21.8 is real: I rebuilt the 21.8 tree from commit 079116e and counted LogSubjectTests at 11 [Fact] + 12 [InlineData] = 23 cases then versus 18 + 34 = 52 cases now, a delta of exactly 29, which accounts for the 2,003 -> 2,032 move (21.8's Passed 1,937 -> 1,966). 4) Corrected-artifact claim: I independently rebuilt the superseded 21.8 candidate from commit 079116e and reproduced its recorded identity (3e59cb06…, 619,636 bytes), then diffed per-entry hashes against the 21.12 archive: only ArrTags.dll differs (1,347,072 / eae2cbabcba9b8ced8f41a55db3d216e020529ce2d567c33f50a2490892b235d -> 1,347,584 / a077a63dd0c4302dc269339a651c5e07530a596611ca94d6a8c886b68bebbbc3); the other six entries are byte-identical, exactly as documented. The only src change between the two commits is the LogSubject.cs SEC-21.5-02/03 fix, so the DLL delta is attributable to the claimed cause. 5) Guard honesty in the docs is good: the release doc states in 'Known environment notes' that no automated test guards byte-identity and that a scripts/pack-release.cs or build-property regression would not fail the suite, limitation P1 says the same, the release checklist that consumes the identity is left unchecked, and the changelog release section explicitly states that no live pinned-host verification of the task 21.12 candidate exists yet and names 21.13/21.14 as the re-derivations — no overstatement of verification for the shipped artifact. check-docs is PASS on every section except the expected contract-interim task-pairing failure for 21.12, and render-docs-state --check is up to date. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding. One open MEDIUM documentation-honesty gap carried forward from 21.8-TQ-1: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md still names the superseded 21.8 identity and now makes a false present-tense equality claim against the release doc and manifest that task 21.12 changed. One open LOW gap: no document states that the release archive is gitignored build output, so the committed manifest checksum is not verifiable from the repository without a rebuild. Also noted informationally: for this build I observed that the tested assembly and the packaged entry are the same bytes, which closes the tested-vs-packaged linkage for this run by observation only, never by a test assertion.

findings.description: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md section 'Corrected v1.2 live matrix (Phase 21 task 21.9)' is a current-state documentation surface that still presents the superseded task 21.8 archive (619,636 bytes, SHA-256 3e59cb06dfd09da4df71e4e4a1c608b664db61326b0184c63cf846fcc502d277, MD5 f3b50a91c7cb63d9560316d8abe2f9dc) with no superseded marker, and it asserts in the present tense: 'The verified identity equals docs/release/build-and-release.md "Release artifact identity" and the manifest.json 1.2.0.0 checksum.' Both of those surfaces now record the task 21.12 identity (2a039fc7… in the release doc, checksum 631fbfa5… in manifest.json), so that equality statement is now false. The historical statement of what task 21.9 ran remains accurate, and the changelog release section correctly and explicitly records that no live verification of the task 21.12 candidate exists yet, so this is not an overclaim that the shipped artifact is live-verified; it is a stale pointer plus a now-false cross-reference that a reader following the testing-host document would use to install the pre-SEC-21.5-02/03 build. The 21.12 worker disclosed this in known_limitations as outside its delegated diff scope and named task 21.13 as the owner; this is the second task in a row leaving the same document unmoved.

findings.description: No document in the current-state tree states that the release archive is gitignored build output, so a reader cannot verify the committed manifest.json checksum without performing a rebuild. The committed manifest.json now records versions[0].checksum 631fbfa5a4fb58fac5a877eeef761193, which refers to artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip — a path excluded by .gitignore and therefore absent from the repository. The release doc states the checksum 'must equal md5sum artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip' as a checklist step, which is a procedure rather than a claim a reader can execute from a clone. The fact is disclosed only in the task 21.12 worker report's known_limitations, and it is pre-existing across 21.3 and 21.8 rather than introduced here. The impact is bounded: the identity is reproducible (I reproduced it from a clean export), and the doc already states the archive is byte-stable across clean builds; the gap is only that the tree does not say the verifying input is absent from the tree.

findings.recommended_action: Add one sentence to docs/release/build-and-release.md's 'Known environment notes' (or to the manifest section) stating that artifacts/ is gitignored build output, that the committed manifest checksum therefore identifies the locally produced archive rather than a file in the tree, and that reproducing it requires './build.sh package' with the pinned SDK. A documentation-maintainer pass is sufficient; no test change is implied.

findings.description: Reproducibility is independently established and honestly presented. My clean export at a path the worker never used reproduced the recorded identity byte-for-byte, so the claim is content-derived rather than path- or commit-derived. The release doc says 'three runs' describing its own evidence, which is true; my run is additional corroboration, not a discrepancy, and the doc does not overstate ('byte-stable across repeated clean builds', demonstrated with the pinned SDK). The absence of a test that guards the identity is stated in both the release doc's 'Known environment notes' and limitation P1, without overclaiming ('a regression in scripts/pack-release.cs or the build properties would not fail the suite'). That equivalence remains an observation, not an assertion any test makes.

findings.description: The skip taxonomy and guard honesty are intact. findings.description: The claimed artifact delta is real and correctly attributed, and the +29 test-total delta is genuine rather than a counting artefact. Rebuilding the task 21.8 tree from commit 079116e reproduced its recorded identity (3e59cb06…, 619,636 bytes) and yields exactly one differing entry against the 21.12 archive: ArrTags.dll 1,347,072 / eae2cbab… -> 1,347,584 / a077a63d…, with the other six entries byte-identical — matching the release doc and the changelog statements. The only src change between the two commits is the LogSubject.cs SEC-21.5-02/03 fix (Path.GetFileName -> ExtractFinalComponent plus the non-printing scalar categories), so the DLL difference is attributable to the claimed cause and not to an unrelated build difference. The test-count delta reconciles exactly: LogSubjectTests went from 11 [Fact] + 12 [InlineData] = 23 cases at 079116e to 18 + 34 = 52 now, a delta of 29, which is precisely the 2,003 -> 2,032 total move and the 1,937 -> 1,966 passed move. The 10 ProviderRedirectTransportTests cases added by 21.7 were already inside 21.8's total. The +29 cases assert observable subject output (final component on both separators, Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp removal, item-id fallback), not restated implementation detail, and the guarded-tier skips are not used to carry a shipped claim.

Golden tests remain fail-closed: RenderGoldenTests has no writer, auto-update, or auto-approval path and compares decoded pixels, dimensions, encoded bytes, output hash, and output fingerprint. Task 21.12 changed no golden and no golden test.

No skip was added or widened: the change set is documentation and manifest only, and git diff over the five guard attribute files since task 21.3 is empty.

No guard-dependent behaviour is claimed verified on the strength of a skipped test: the release doc scopes the host-guarded tier to assembly reflection, and the changelog release section states that no live pinned-host verification of the task 21.12 candidate exists yet (21.13 pending).
determinism_checked: Task 21.12's diff is documentation and manifest only: git status --short shows M PLANS.md, M docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md, M docs/plan/state.json, M docs/release/build-and-release.md, M manifest.json, plus the new untracked docs/implementation/21.12/ report directory; git diff --stat is 5 files, 180 insertions, 103 deletions. No source, test, golden, project, or build-metadata file changed, so no suite determinism or isolation property could have changed.

Independent clean-export build at a path the worker did not use reproduced the recorded SHA-256, MD5, and 619,861-byte size, and cmp against the repository archive is clean, so the identity is content-derived rather than path- or commit-derived.
Archive entries are stamped 2000-01-01 00:00 in ordinal order, produced by scripts/pack-release.cs, so timestamp and enumeration order are not sources of variance.

The suite is order-independent and shares no mutable state observable in these runs; the four tiers each ran green from a freshly built tree, and the archive-presence variants (1,966 vs 1,963) differ only by the three documented packaging facts.

scripts/check-docs.sh passes every content section ('generated status blocks are current; plan state is consistent' with dotnet on PATH, artifact identity agrees, doc budget, current-state links) and fails only the expected contract-interim task-pairing lines for 21.12, which clear when the implementation-reviewer report is added and listed; 'dotnet run scripts/render-docs-state.cs -- --check' reports 'PLANS.md and state.json agree'.
limitations: No automated test guards the archive byte-identity or the manifest checksum; reproducibility and identity rest on the recorded multi-run clean-build evidence, which I corroborated with an independent fourth run. This is stated in docs/release/build-and-release.md 'Known environment notes' and limitation P1 without overclaiming, and it is a pre-existing boundary, not something task 21.12 introduced.

I did not modify any test, source, build-metadata, or documentation file; this audit ran builds and suites only in disposable exports under /tmp/final-review/test-quality/ and in the repository's existing artifacts/ output.

scripts/check-docs.sh currently reports the contract-interim pairing failure for task 21.12 (worker report present, implementation-reviewer report not yet on disk / not yet listed in state.json reports). That is the contract-defined interim state recorded by tasks 21.1, 21.2, 21.3, 21.7, 21.8, and 21.11, not a defect of this task.

The forced-native tier I reproduced uses the pinned host's native dependency chain rather than the task 21.8 probe sysroot, so it validates that the tier passes and that the counts match the doc, not that the two environments are equivalent to one another.

The corrected v1.2 artifact has no live pinned-host end-to-end verification at this point; the changelog release section says so explicitly and names task 21.13 as the re-derivation. I did not run the live matrix (out of scope for this task).
Finding 21.12-TQ-1 remains open and is owned by task 21.13 or a documentation-maintainer pass; finding 21.12-TQ-2 is a pre-existing LOW documentation gap disclosed only in the worker report.
